**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity)**

The second Section 12.4 (`p0046`) binds *us*, not the Vendor: "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

This breaches the rule in two independent walk-away respects — a post-term non-compete of 24 months (double the 12-month ceiling) and wholly undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor," "any territory"). It also sweeps in acquisitions and internal development, which the fallback would have to carve out. Separately, it flatly contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," so the clause is internally inconsistent as well as unacceptable.

Redline validated (`ok:true`): delete `p0046` in full, reaching the preferred position with the smallest possible edit. The comment offers the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, ≤12 months, carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions) in case Vendor raises a genuine protection need.

Note for the wider review: Section 12.4 (the first one, `sec-12.4`) contains a separate 24-month no-hire restriction on Customer, and Section 7.2 contains a disclose-and-match obligation — both also cut against Section 12.3, but they fall under other playbook rules rather than NONCOMPETE.
